metaDescription: Seminole, the Gaines County seat, sits near the giant Wasson Field alongside newer horizontal drilling. Get an honest valuation on your interest.
heroLead: Seminole is the Gaines County seat, and the ground around it carries two very different oil stories: the old giant Wasson Field to the north, and newer horizontal Wolfcamp development spreading through the rest of the county.
intro: Wasson Field, straddling the Gaines-Yoakum county line, has been one of the larger oil fields in the entire Permian Basin since its discovery in the 1930s, and it's spent decades under waterflood and enhanced recovery. If your family's minerals near Seminole sit within or near that footprint, expect a different production story than a newer horizontal unit elsewhere in the county.

sections.heading: Wasson Field's long, mature production life
paragraphs: Wasson has been under secondary and tertiary recovery for so long that current output per well is generally modest and steady rather than the sharp initial spike you'd see from a new horizontal completion. Leases here have typically been held by production for decades, and mineral ownership has often passed through multiple generations without lapsing.

sections.heading: Newer development elsewhere in Gaines County
paragraphs: Away from the Wasson footprint, Gaines County has seen some of the densest horizontal Wolfcamp and Bone Spring drilling anywhere in the Permian over the past decade. If your interest is outside the old field boundary, it may be part of a much more active, higher-decline unit than an owner sitting inside Wasson.

sections.heading: Seminole as the county's hub
paragraphs: As the Gaines County seat, Seminole is where the courthouse records for the whole surrounding area live, and it's also where a lot of the operators active in both the Wasson footprint and the newer horizontal acreage keep field offices. That mix of old and new industry presence is part of what keeps Seminole functioning as a real oilfield town rather than a place that boomed once and moved on.

For owners, that ongoing presence generally means your interest, wherever it sits in the county, is being watched by more than one operator, which supports a competitive valuation when it comes time to sell.

faqs.question: Is my Seminole-area interest tied to Wasson Field or newer drilling?
faqs.answer: It depends on your specific tract's location. Wasson production is mature secondary recovery; acreage outside the field boundary is more likely tied to recent horizontal development. We check your section specifically before answering.

faqs.question: My checks from Wasson Field have been small and steady for years. Is the interest still worth much?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, given the long production history behind it. We factor decades of production history into the valuation rather than relying on the current check size alone.

faqs.question: How active is drilling around Seminole right now?
faqs.answer: Gaines County overall has remained one of the more heavily permitted counties in Texas. We check current activity near your specific tract to confirm what applies to your interest.
